narrative: The system estimated your chance of becoming a bad credit risk at 27.0%. That is not a certainty, but under the bank’s decision rule it was high enough to decline the application. The strongest factor behind this outcome was the size of the loan you requested. At 11,054 DM, it is far above the average approved request of about 3,020 DM, so the system saw substantially more exposure than it is used to approving. The next most influential factor was your checking account situation. Having no checking account recorded was not treated as a major warning; in fact, it helped move the decision toward good credit. The third factor was your savings profile. An unknown or no-savings status also worked slightly in your favor, rather than against you. Even so, those two positive signals were not enough to offset the much stronger concern created by the large requested amount. Other details, such as a 36-month term compared with an approved average near 19 months and a credit history described as critical or other credits, likely added to the cautious view. To improve your chances, consider applying for a smaller amount closer to the typical approved level, shortening the repayment period, providing a guarantor or co-applicant, and documenting stable income, savings, or collateral. You could also ask the bank which specific cutoff you missed and whether a revised request would be reviewed.
